findings.location: service composition around lines 344-359; PreparedPass1DispatchWorker.ExecuteAsync; repository-wide production call graph
findings.affected_requirement: Story 12.3 first acceptance group; FR-004, FR-006, FR-007, FR-032, FR-040 through FR-052; SC-001, SC-007, SC-010, SC-011, SC-012
findings.evidence: The public Start endpoint calls only IPreparedPass1Store.StartAsync, which creates the durable pair and jobs. No production component calls ClaimNextAsync, builds a dispatch request from a claimed lease, invokes PreparedPass1DispatchWorker, commits parsed output through IPass1CodeLogicDocumentCommitter, records dispatch failures, or invokes ReconcileAsync when jobs become terminal. Program.cs registers the store, navigation service, and coordinator but registers neither IPreparedPass1JobExecutor, IPreparedPass1WorkerDispatcher, PreparedPass1DispatchWorker, nor IPass1CodeLogicDocumentCommitter. Repository-wide production references show ClaimNextAsync, RecordFailureAsync, and ReconcileAsync only as port/implementation declarations, while PreparedPass1DispatchWorker is an uncalled wrapper for a caller-supplied already-claimed batch. Therefore an authenticated Start can remain indefinitely Running with Pending jobs and cannot produce a Code Logic Document through production composition.
findings.correction_outcome: Return to the architecture owner to define and then implement the missing production execution coordinator: claim only through the durable pair lease seam, build one server-owned packet for that claim, invoke the closed Worker executor, commit or durably classify its result, continue under the shared limit, and trigger terminal reconciliation. Register every concrete production dependency and prove Start-to-terminal behavior without adding Story 12.4 or automatic background resume.

findings.location: PreparedPass1ProviderAvailabilityProbe lines 15-38 and ResumeAsync lines 229-252; PreparedPass1Store.ProbeProviderAsync around line 1829
findings.affected_requirement: Story 12.3 provider-unavailable acceptance group; FR-037 through FR-039, FR-043, FR-044; SC-008
findings.evidence: PreparedPass1ProviderAvailabilityProbe considers the provider available when WorkerAgentProviderResolver can resolve configuration; it performs no fixed source-free provider request. WorkerAgentProviderHealthProbe implements timing calculations only. ProbeProviderAsync can transition durable probe state, but no production caller invokes it. Consequently an opened provider circuit cannot execute the required five active probes or autonomously reach PausedProviderUnavailable after the fifth failed window; manual Resume may also close recovery based on configuration resolution even when the endpoint remains unavailable.
findings.correction_outcome: Implement and compose the accepted fixed source-free provider health request and a durable probe driver that invokes ProbeProviderAsync exactly at the eligible 10, 30, 60, 120, and 300 second windows, preserves Retry-After bounds, stops claims while probing, and persists PausedProviderUnavailable after failure five. Add production-composition tests using an unavailable endpoint, not only direct store method calls.

findings.location: GetAsync lines 24-105 and navigation receipt CommitAsync lines 163-256; PreparedNavigateCodeBinding lines 11-15
findings.affected_requirement: FR-011, FR-014, FR-017, FR-018, FR-035, FR-044; SC-003, SC-004, SC-007; Navigation Session definition
findings.evidence: The navigation binding carries only JobId, ToolAttemptOrdinal, and SourceFileCodeUnitId. GetAsync reconstructs Repository/Profiled Revision inventory and budgets but does not require the job to be Running, verify a current lease token or lease expiry, or require the pair to be Running with a closed circuit. Receipt CommitAsync locks only the navigation budget and likewise does not revalidate job ownership or pair phase. A stale Worker continuation holding job identities can therefore obtain revision-bound evidence and consume durable navigation budget after its lease expires, after another Worker owns the job, or while the pair is paused/terminal. Later Document commit rejection does not undo the source disclosure or receipt mutation.
findings.correction_outcome: Bind navigation to the server-held current lease identity and expected job version, and atomically revalidate Running state, unexpired lease ownership, pair phase/circuit, Repository/Profiled Revision, and budget before returning evidence or committing any receipt. Add expired-lease, replaced-owner, paused-circuit, completed-job, and terminal-pair nondisclosure tests.

findings.affected_requirement: FR-032 through FR-035; SC-006, SC-007; Story 12.1 durable-scan-contracts Atomic result commit step 2
findings.evidence: The completed replay branch compares the job, current Logical Document pointer, DocumentVersion scalar/content fields, and incoming durable bindings, but it never reconstructs or compares the persisted Source Anchors, Document Sections, Index Entry, or direct REFERENCES Edge cardinality/content for the committed source Document. DurableBindingsMatchAsync validates current inputs, receipts, classifications, and referenced targets rather than the already-persisted source graph. Deleting or corrupting an associated graph row can therefore still return Replayed, contrary to the inherited requirement that replay compare the associated canonical Document graph and reject missing, changed, or duplicate linkage.
findings.correction_outcome: Reconstruct the complete persisted canonical graph for the completed Document Version and require exact identities, ordering, content, and cardinalities for anchors, sections, index, and direct Edges before returning replay. Any missing, changed, reordered, or duplicate relation must conflict or fail integrity without mutation. Add row-removal, row-mutation, and duplicate-cardinality PostgreSQL replay tests.

findings.location: composition checks around lines 117-130; Pass1HostRuntimeQualificationTests lines 18-105
findings.affected_requirement: SC-008 and SC-012; plan Verification Strategy and real host qualification
findings.evidence: The production-boundary qualification checks constructor shapes, literals, endpoint registration, navigate_code registration, and coordinator registration, but does not require a registered Worker executor, dispatcher, commit port, execution driver, or probe driver. The host-runtime qualification verifies tool versions, hashes, JDT-LS factory construction, and PostgreSQL 17 connectivity but does not execute an approved two-manifest Pass 1 from authenticated Start through claimed jobs, Worker results, immutable Documents, and reconciliation. These tests therefore passed while the production pipeline and probe loop were unreachable. The verification artifact also truthfully records that the unfiltered full suite was not green, so it cannot supply the missing end-to-end evidence.
findings.correction_outcome: Add a production-composed integration test that resolves the real DI graph and drives two approved Prepared Scan Manifests through Start, claims, bounded Worker execution, document commits, failure/retry policy, reconciliation, and terminal status. Add a provider-outage path through the same composition. Retain the current runtime/version checks as supporting evidence rather than treating them as execution proof.

summary: REVISE. The pinned candidate contains substantial isolated store, navigation, projection, migration, API, and qualification work, and the reviewed host-runtime and exclusion evidence is appropriately bounded. However, four High findings prevent acceptance: the production Start path is not connected to durable claim/Worker/commit/reconciliation execution; the five provider probes have no active production implementation or caller; navigate_code is not bound to current lease ownership; and completed replay does not verify the persisted associated Document graph required by the inherited Story 12.1 contract. Existing tests exercise isolated seams and static composition but do not cover a production-composed Start-to-terminal Pass 1, allowing these gaps to pass. No files, lifecycle state, staging, or Git history were modified during this review.
